shots.phrase: Every oscillating mechanical system has ways it naturally prefers to move.
Push a swing slowly, or far too quickly, and the motion stays modest.
Push near its natural rhythm and each input can reinforce the motion already underway.
A frequency-response plot puts driving frequency on the horizontal axis and response amplitude on the vertical axis.
The peak marks the resonant region.
Its location and width tell engineers which excitations are most dangerous or most useful.
Real systems lose energy through damping, so their response does not grow without bound.
Engineers can add damping, change stiffness or mass, or keep operating speeds away from a troublesome natural frequency.
The practical lesson is simple: resonance is not automatically failure, but ignoring the frequency relationship can turn a small repeating force into a large motion.
